name: Clota

attributes.attribute: goddess of the River Clyde and its fertility
river in Scotland that carries the goddess's name
spring nymphs who are the Continental form of Clota

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Clota was a goddess of the Scottish land. Her name belongs to the River Clyde in Scotland. She stood for the river and for the fertility of its watershed. On the Continent she also appeared as the spring nymphs called the Clutoida.

okr.objective: Clota is the Scottish goddess of the River Clyde and the fertility of its land.
key_results: Clota gives her name to the River Clyde.
She stands for the fertility of the river's watershed.
On the Continent she appears as the Clutoida spring nymphs.
